title: Check yourself: Layered guardrails, monitoring and the practice

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team wants to spot a user who keeps probing the application's guardrails. Which monitoring rule fits?

options.text: Alert on every question put to a person, since each may be an attack
options.says: Ruled out because "An `ask` is the gate working, and alerts on it bury the real ones."

options.text: Add up denials across all actors, and alert on the total
options.says: Ruled out because the alert is per actor: "three denials by one actor", and a pooled total names nobody.

options.text: Count denials for each actor, and alert at a threshold
options.says: The page says the response to repeat offenders "needs a threshold", and "The practice uses three denials by one actor, which raises an alert".

options.text: Tighten the system prompt, so the model refuses harder next time
options.says: Ruled out because "A control that blocks should also record", and a stricter prompt records nothing.

questions.stem: A team wants to cut the risk of a prompt leak without hurting the work. Which step adds no complexity?

options.text: Screen every reply with a prompted model that looks for leaked text
options.says: Ruled out because the page ranks it behind the cheapest step: "The cheapest to apply is the third, because it adds no complexity."

options.text: Add many rules that forbid repeating text from the instructions
options.says: Ruled out because leak-proofing "can add complexity that may degrade performance".

options.text: Rewrite the prompt with tighter wording before any monitoring
options.says: Ruled out because the first advice is to "try monitoring before prompt engineering".

options.text: Leave out proprietary details that the task does not need
options.says: The page says "If Claude doesn't need it to perform the task, don't include it", and that a secret not in the prompt "cannot leak from it".

questions.stem: A gate writes each decision to an audit with the call's inputs, one of which is an API key. What should it record?

options.text: The arguments, with the secret replaced by a fixed marker
options.says: The page says to record "the arguments with secrets redacted, because a log that holds a raw key has become a leak of its own".

options.text: The raw arguments, since an audit wants the full detail
options.says: Ruled out because the audit keeps "the arguments with secrets redacted" and not the raw ones.

options.text: No entry for a call that happens to carry a secret value
options.says: Ruled out because the audit exists to answer "who tried what, which denials repeat, which sessions were tainted", and a call that carries a secret is one worth recording.

options.text: The tool and the decision, with the arguments left out entirely
options.says: Ruled out because the record holds "the tool, the decision, the reason and the arguments with secrets redacted", so the arguments stay in it.
